name: Domain specific reputation

subjectOf.text: Reputation tokens must have their power limited to their proper domain: for each different expertise there must be a separate type of non-interchangeable reputation token, so that a token carries power only within the DAO whose members hold that specific skill.
subjectOf.abstract: Reputation tokens need to have power limited to their proper domain, meaning that for each different expertise, there is a separate type of non-interchangeable reputa- tion token.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, The Importance of Reputation for the Evolution of Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782210
scope_conditions: organizations spanning multiple domains of expertise

subjectOf.text: Reputation in the underlying system is domain-specific and strictly non-transferable: bound to the holder's identity, earned only through validated work, and incapable of sale, loan or transfer.
subjectOf.abstract: Should intelligent agents have legal rights? This Article sets that question aside and asks a smaller one that matters more in practice. An intelligent agent that earns a reputation record has something to lose.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Should an Intelligent Agent Have Legal Rights? (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7596939

subjectOf.text: Three validator families share a mean accuracy of 0.75 while differing in structure: one is homogeneous at 0.75, one has each validator reliable at 0.90 on two hash-drawn tags and at 0.60 on the other two so that domain-scoped reputation has something to find, and one has five validators at 0.90 and fifteen at 0.70, a competent minority.
subjectOf.abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518
scope_conditions: The validators are simulated and err independently given their accuracy, which depends only on the tag.
The families are a property of the design, fixed before any run.
